podcast.title: "The List" of Venues
podcast.body: D.O.A. compiled and traded "the list," which was a growing catalog of punk-friendly venues and places to stay across North America. This list was shared among dozens, if not hundreds, of like-minded bands, significantly expanding the reach of punk and hardcore across the continent. "DOA compiled something called the list. This was a growing list of punk-friendly venues and places to stay across North America that was made available and then traded among dozens, maybe hundreds of other like-minded bands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Coined "Hardcore" Term
podcast.body: D.O.A. is credited with giving the new, harder, faster, louder, and more aggressive form of punk its name. They achieved this with the release of their second album, "Hardcore 81," on April 22, 1981, after which the term caught on and became the official name for the subgenre. "Second, it was DOA that gave this new, harder, faster, louder and more aggressive form of punk its name. On April 22, 1981, the group released their second album. They called it Hardcore 81 and then they toured the hell out of it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Godfathers of Hardcore
podcast.body: Hailing from Vancouver, D.O.A. are considered the godfathers of the hardcore genre. Their album "Hardcore 81" was instrumental in popularizing the term and sound. The band's music exemplified early hardcore's strong anti-establishment stance. "And now they're considered to be the godfathers of the genre."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: West Coast Touring Strategy
podcast.body: D.O.A., based in Vancouver, primarily toured north-south along the West Coast from San Diego to Vancouver, finding it easier and more affordable than east-west travel due to the Rocky Mountains. They would then head east once they got south. "Vancouver's DOA was very much part of this and while they did tour through Canada, it was often easier to go up and down the west coast playing the same gigs as their hardcore brother."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
